sections.text: The SessionFS API server exposes a REST API for session management, auditing, sync, and settings.

sections.heading: Base URL
sections.text: Cloud: https://api.sessionfs.dev Self-hosted: Your deployment URL

sections.heading: Authentication
sections.text: All endpoints (except signup) require a Bearer token: Authorization: Bearer sk_sfs_... Two key kinds: User keys — created via POST /api/v1/auth/keys. Tied to a single user, inherit all of that user's permissions. Legacy keys are back-filled to scopes=["*"]. Service keys (v0.10.10+) — created via POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/service-keys. Org-scoped, expirable, and restricted to an enumerated scopes list (e.g. ["handoffs:write", "agent_runs:write"]). Deny-by-default: a service key only reaches a route handler that explicitly opted in via require_scope(...). The recommended credential for cloud agents (Bedrock, Vertex), CI runners (GitHub Actions, GitLab MR), and integration partners. Structured 401/403 error codes: api_key_revoked, api_key_expired, service_key_not_allowed, insufficient_scope (with required + current arrays), cross_org_denied, service_key_project_required, service_key_project_not_registered, service_key_project_ambiguous.

sections.heading: Service Keys (v0.10.10+)
sections.text: Org-scoped, scope-restricted API keys for cloud agents, CI runners, and integration partners. Org admin role + Team+ tier required for mutations. Raw key returned exactly once on create + rotate; the list endpoint only returns key_prefix. | Method | Path | Auth | Description | | POST | /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/service-keys | Bearer (org admin) | Create a service key (body: name, scopes[], optional expires_at, project_ids[]) | | GET | /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/service-keys | Bearer (org member) | List service keys for the org | | DELETE | /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/service-keys/{id} | Bearer (org admin) | Revoke a service key (body: optional revoke_reason) | | POST | /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/service-keys/{id}/rotate | Bearer (org admin) | Issue a new raw secret for an existing key | Available scopes (the * wildcard is reserved for legacy user/admin keys; service keys must enumerate explicitly): | Scope | Status | Routes opted in | | handoffs:read, handoffs:write | ✅ live (v0.10.10) | Handoff create/claim/revoke/decline + comments + events | | agent_runs:write | ✅ live (v0.10.10) | POST /agent-runs, POST /agent-runs/{id}/complete, POST /agent-runs/{id}/usage | | tickets:read, tickets:write | ✅ live (v0.10.18) | Ticket list/get/comments/review-state/readiness + start/complete/comment | | meetings:read, meetings:write | ✅ live (v0.29.0) | Stored meeting transcripts: upload/list/get/delete + participant resolution (see Meetings) | | knowledge:read, knowledge:write | ✅ live (v0.10.19; project context + wiki since v0.29.1) | Knowledge entries: GET /entries, GET /entries/{id}, POST /entries/add, PUT /entries/{id} (dismiss/update/refresh/promote/supersede). Project context (knowledge:read): GET /projects/{id}, GET /projects/{id}/context/sections/{slug}. Wiki (knowledge:read): list/get pages, page history and backlinks; (knowledge:write): PUT /projects/{id}/pages/{slug} — writes record actor_type="service_key" + service_key_id/service_key_name | | personas:read, personas:write | ✅ live (v0.10.20) | Persona list/get + create/update/delete | | agent_runs:read | ✅ live (v0.10.21) | GET /agent-runs, GET /agent-runs/{run_id} | | loops:read, loops:write | ✅ live (v0.29.2) | Review loops: GET /projects/{id}/loops, GET /projects/{id}/loops/{loop_id}, POST /projects/{id}/loops, PATCH /projects/{id}/loops/{loop_id}, plus the loop report, insights, story and checklist routes (see Review Loop API). User keys also need editor standing; cost_budget_usd is org-admin only, and service keys never see or set dollars | | agent_feedback:read, agent_feedback:write | ✅ live (v0.17) | GET /agent-feedback, GET /agent-feedback/summary, POST /agent-feedback | | marketplace:read, marketplace:write | ✅ live (v0.16) | Marketplace search/inspect/download/feed + personal package/registry publishing | | skills:read, skills:request, skills:approve, skills:admin | ✅ live (v0.16) | Approved instruction load, install-request lifecycle, org registries/packages/assignments | | skills_verify:run | ✅ live (platform, tier-coupled) | The works-in harness protocol (claim / projection / result). Only a platform admin may mint or rotate a key with it, and the key works only while the user it runs as and the admin who minted or last rotated it are both still active platform admins | | skills_registry:poll | ✅ live (platform, tier-coupled) | The registry poller's scheduler credential (POST /api/v1/admin/skills/registries/poll). Only a platform admin may mint or rotate a key with it, and the key works only while the user it runs as and the admin who minted or last rotated it are both still active platform admins | | platform_sweeps:run | ✅ live (platform, tier-coupled) | The scheduled sweeps' credential: catalog regenerate, verify sweep, freshness sweep, rescan, publisher recheck, the GitHub webhook-delivery sweep, and (v0.23.0) the KB compile, org digest and helper retention sweeps. Only a platform admin may mint or rotate a key with it, and the key works only while the user it runs as and the admin who minted or last rotated it are both still active platform admins | | admin_metrics:read | ✅ live (platform, tier-coupled, v0.23.0) | GET /api/v1/admin/metrics (Prometheus). Only a platform admin may mint or rotate a key with it, and the key works only while the user it runs as and the admin who minted or last rotated it are both still active platform admins | | sessions:read, rules:read, rules:write, retrieval_audit:read, admin:* | Reserved | Not yet opted in on any route | Tier-coupled scopes. The four platform scopes above are *tier-coupled*: they are mint/rotate-only by a platform admin and the key keeps working only while both the user it runs as and the admin who minted or last rotated it are still active platform admins. Demoting or deactivating either one stops the key with a 403 that names the minter's current tier and the fix (restore the minter, or mint a new key as a user who stays a platform admin). Minting and rotating a tier-coupled key returns a warnings array with a minter_tier_coupling entry so the operator knows before they build a job around it, and service-keys list exposes coupling_ok (true/false/null) plus coupling_reason so a silently-broken key is visible. Making someone a platform admin just long enough to mint a key doesn't work: the key stops as soon as they're demoted (v0.28.0 makes this visible; the rule itself is unchanged).

Not found and no access both return 404 (v0.25.0) | | GET | /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets/{tid} | Bearer (tickets:read) | Get a ticket with dependencies, dependents, and recent comments. Includes created_by and resolved_by (name and persona), due_date and estimated_effort (v0.28.0) | | GET | /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets/{tid}/events | Bearer (tickets:read) | The ticket's change history, newest first: each event has action, field, before, after, actor and created_at. Query: limit (1–200, default 50) and before (an event id; pass next_before from the previous page) (v0.28.0) | | PUT | /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets/{tid} | Bearer (tickets:write) | Partial mutation for title / description / priority / acceptance_criteria / context_refs / file_refs / depends_on / assigned_user (teammate email or user id, null to unassign; v0.27.0) / due_date / estimated_effort (null clears either; v0.28.0). Status transitions remain FSM-only. Authz: creator OR project admin. Optional lease_epoch for optimistic concurrency (409 + structured envelope on stale; last-write-wins when omitted; lease_epoch alone rejected with 400 — it's a fence, not a mutation). Side effect: every successful update auto-posts ONE author_persona='system' diff comment + writes per-field rows to the ticket_edits audit table (no-op writes don't pollute the audit). depends_on updates run same-project + cycle + dedup validation before wipe-and-reinsert. sections.heading: Meetings (v0.29.0)
sections.text: Stored meeting transcripts (GitHub #116). A meeting belongs to exactly one project or one group; project meetings admit service keys via meetings:read / meetings:write, while group meetings require a user key (Team+). Uploads are DLP-scanned under the strictest union of the caller's orgs and the scope org; a block-mode policy rejects with 422 dlp_blocked, and every other mode (redact, warn, or no policy) redacts secrets before storage. sections.text: Project groups are org-scoped flat collections of projects (Team+). sections.heading: Skills Marketplace
sections.text: y listing, including public ones) and block the bytes everywhere; org owners/admins (or a personal package's owner) moderate only their own non-public listings and never a public listing; personal owners may yank but not block. A platform takedown can only be restored by a platform admin; a platform admin may also lift an owner takedown. A restore lifts only the blocks this target itself placed: a target blocked only because a block on identical content elsewhere applies to it returns 409 blocked_by_other_target (restore that block instead). Taken-down listings are refused everywhere (404). Blocking also revokes install approvals, consent receipts and org assignments of the affected copies (marked, not deleted; a restore does not re-grant) and adds the bytes to a durable content-hash blocklist that survives version deletion: blocked bytes are refused at publish (403 content_blocked) and on every delivery path. A platform block applies everywhere; an org block applies only to that org's non-public listings. User keys only | | POST | /api/v1/marketplace/packages/{package_id}/yank · /block · /restore | skills:admin | Same for a whole package, including versions published later (an owner's package action covers only the package's non-public listings). While a package is platform-blocked, publishing into it returns 403 package_blocked and none of its versions can be deleted | | GET | /api/v1/marketplace/revocations | skills:read | Revocations feed: ?since=<iso>&limit= (≤ 500) → {"revocations":[{"package_id","version_id","content_hash","state","reason","changed_at","kind","block_scope","scope_org_id"}],"next_since":"<iso>","has_more":bool}, oldest first. Echo next_since back as since; event timestamps are unique and strictly increasing, so paging never skips or repeats. kind is version, package (version_id/content_hash null) or content (a blocked or unblocked content hash; package_id/version_id null). block_scope is global for a platform block (or its restore), org for an org owner/admin's block (or its restore), owner for an owner-layer yank (or its restore) by an org owner/admin or a personal package's owner, and null for a platform yank (or its restore). org and owner entries apply only to copies installed from a non-public listing of that package/version; an owner never takes down a public listing (only a platform admin does). scope_org_id is the owning org for org (always set) and owner entries (null for a personal package), and null otherwise; when set, also require the copy's owner_org_id to match. Version and package events are scoped to listings you can see; a global content block reaches every caller, with a generic reason unless you can see the moderated listing; an org content block reaches that org's members | Grant list pages and incompleteness. The install-request list and both assignment lists are keyset-paginated: pass limit (1–500, default 100) and cursor (the previous page's next_cursor). Every response is {"items": [...], "incomplete": bool, "omitted_count": int, "has_more": bool, "next_cursor": str|null, "generation": str} (the install-request list also carries can_approve). Pages are in a stable id order; keep requesting with cursor=next_cursor until has_more is false - only then is the set complete. A page can hold fewer than limit items (filters and omitted records). An invalid cursor is a 422. generation is an opaque token for the collection's state, carried inside every cursor: if anything in the collection changes while you page (a grant created, decided, revoked or deleted, a membership change for the caller's assignment list, or a moderation action affecting one of its versions), the next page returns 409 listing_changed - restart from the first page. The lists never guess a grant's targeting: a stored record whose target_tools or requested_capabilities is not a list of known names is omitted from its page, and that page reports incomplete: true with the count in omitted_count; treat the whole set as incomplete if any page was. Fetching or approving such a record directly returns 500 grant_record_corrupt, and it never grants anything.

sections.heading: OpenAPI
sections.text: After deployment, interactive API docs are available at: Swagger UI: https://your-domain/api/docs ReDoc: https://your-domain/api/redoc
Automatic session syncing so you never lose work. The daemon pushes sessions to the cloud automatically, with configurable modes.

sections.heading: Modes
sections.text: | Mode | Behavior | | off (default) | Manual sync only. Run sfs push explicitly. | | all | Every new or updated session auto-pushes to cloud. | | selective | Only sessions in the watchlist auto-push. |

sections.heading: Enable autosync
sections.text: sfs sync auto --mode all

sections.heading: Selective mode
sections.text: sfs sync auto --mode selective sfs sync watch ses_abc ses_def # Add to watchlist sfs sync unwatch ses_abc # Remove from watchlist sfs sync watchlist # Show watched sessions

sections.heading: Check status
sections.text: sfs sync status

sections.heading: Sync-aware deletes
sections.text: Sessions you delete stay deleted -- autosync respects your intent. When you run sfs delete, the session is added to a local exclusion list and autosync skips it in both push and pull directions. See Delete Lifecycle for the full model.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Daemon detects session changes via filesystem events Changes are debounced (30 seconds default) to avoid hammering the API Session is packed and pushed with ETag conflict detection If offline, changes are queued and retried with exponential backoff

sections.heading: Configuration
sections.text: In ~/.sessionfs/config.toml: [sync] auto = "all" debounce = 30 Or via the dashboard under Settings → Sync (propagates to daemon within 60 seconds).
SessionFS billing is managed through SessionFS Cloud. Self-hosted customers do not run billing infrastructure.

sections.heading: Start with cloud
sections.text: Create an account at app.sessionfs.dev. The dashboard creates your API key, walks you through setup, and lets you upgrade when you need cloud sync, shared knowledge, or team coordination.

sections.heading: Plans
sections.text: | Tier | Price | Best for | Key features | | Free | $0 | Local development | Capture, resume, local search, local MCP | | Starter | $4.99/mo | Solo cloud sync | Cloud sync, dashboard, bookmarks, manual Judge, deterministic summaries | | Pro | $14.99/mo | Solo agent memory | Starter + autosync, remote MCP, project context, knowledge base, rules portability, DLP, agent personas | | Team | $14.99/user/mo | Shared agent coordination | Pro + org management, shared storage pool, tickets, team handoff, shared personas, project groups with restricted visibility, weekly org activity digest | | Enterprise | Custom | Governed AI agent operations | Team + self-hosted or single-tenant deployment, HIPAA DLP, SSO, audit retention, AgentRun CI enforcement, cloud agent support, session helper, two-way Jira Cloud sync, Confluence publishing | See Pricing for the current public plan summary.

sections.heading: Cloud storage
sections.text: | Tier | Cloud storage | | Free | 50 MB sync limit | | Starter | 500 MB | | Pro | 2 GB | | Team | 1 GB per seat, pooled | | Enterprise | Custom | Each session upload is also capped: 50 MB on Free and 300 MB on every paid plan. If a session is larger, the server rejects the upload with a clear error naming your plan's limit; upgrade for a larger per-session limit.

sections.heading: Manage a subscription
sections.text: Billing changes happen in the dashboard: Open app.sessionfs.dev. Open Billing (under Manage in the sidebar). Choose a plan or open the subscription page for invoices, payment methods, upgrades, downgrades, and cancellation. Team billing is owned by organization admins. Members inherit the organization's tier and storage pool.

sections.heading: Self-hosted and enterprise
sections.text: Self-hosted customers do not configure billing infrastructure in their cluster. Enterprise billing, renewals, and licensed features are handled through your SessionFS agreement. For self-hosted deployments, the runtime receives its allowed tier from the license system. The application should be deployed with the license material provided by SessionFS, not with any customer-operated checkout, subscription, or payment-webhook configuration. Talk to Enterprise if you need self-hosted, single-tenant, HIPAA-oriented, or custom-retention deployment.

sections.heading: License activation
sections.text: Enterprise customers who receive a license key can activate it from the dashboard. The activating user confirms the previewed organization and tier, then confirms a single-use, time-limited code sent to their email address — activation completes only after this email verification step, and the activating user becomes the owner of the newly created organization. See Organizations → Self-service license activation for the full flow. An organization's plan, seats, and storage are resolved from a single authoritative entitlement record, so an activated license is the org-wide source of truth for what the org is licensed to use.
Complete reference for all sfs commands.

sections.heading: Global Options
sections.text: sfs [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]... | Option | Description | | --help | Show help and exit | | --version, -V | Show the installed version (sessionfs X.Y.Z (python …, platform arch)) and exit. Also available as sfs version. |

sections.heading: sfs list
sections.text: List captured sessions. sfs list [OPTIONS] | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --tool | string | — | Filter by source tool (e.g., claude-code) | | --since | string | — | Show sessions since time (7d, 24h, or ISO date) | | --tag | string | — | Filter by tag | | --sort | string | recent | Sort order: recent, oldest, messages, tokens | | --json | flag | false | Output as JSON | | --quiet, -q | flag | false | Only print session IDs | Example: $ sfs list --since 7d --sort tokens Sessions (5) ┌──────────────┬─────────────┬────────┬──────────┬───────────┐ │ ID │ Tool │ Model │ Messages │ Title │ ├──────────────┼─────────────┼────────┼──────────┼───────────┤ │ a1b2c3d4e5f6 │ claude-code │ opus-4 │ 23 │ Debug ... │ └──────────────┴─────────────┴────────┴──────────┴───────────┘

sections.heading: sfs show
sections.text: Show session details. sfs show SESSION_ID [OPTIONS] | Argument | Required | Description | | SESSION_ID | yes | Session ID or prefix (min 4 chars) | | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --messages, -m | flag | false | Show conversation messages | | --cost, -c | flag | false | Show cost estimate | | --page-size | int | 20 | Messages per page (with --messages) | Example: $ sfs show a1b2 --cost ╭──────────── Session Details ────────────╮ │ Session ID: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-... │ │ Title: Debug auth flow │ │ Tool: claude-code 1.0.23 │ │ Model: claude-opus-4 (anthropic) │ │ Messages: 23 │ │ Input tokens: 34,200 │ │ Output tokens: 12,800 │ ╰─────────────────────────────────────────╯ ╭──────────── Cost Estimate ──────────────╮ │ Input cost: $0.5130 │ │ Output cost: $0.9600 │ │ Total: $1.4730 │ ╰─────────────────────────────────────────╯

sections.heading: sfs resume
sections.text: Resume a captured session in any supported AI tool. sfs resume SESSION_ID [OPTIONS] | Argument | Required | Description | | SESSION_ID | yes | Session ID or prefix | | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --project | path | — | Target project path (overrides workspace) | | --in | string | claude-code | Target tool: claude-code, codex, copilot, or gemini | | --model, -m | string | — | Model to use in target tool (e.g. gpt-4.1, claude-sonnet-4, gemini-2.5-pro) | | --no-rules-sync | flag | false | Skip preflight of the target tool's project rules file. Per-invocation only. | | --force-rules | flag | false | Overwrite an unmanaged target-tool rules file with SessionFS-managed content. One-time permission — the file becomes SessionFS-managed afterward and subsequent resumes refresh it normally. | Converts the session to the target tool's native format and injects it into that tool's session storage. Cursor, Cline, Roo Code, Kilo Code, Antigravity, and Amp are capture-only — --in cursor (and the others) is rejected with an error. Use --in with one of the four supported resume targets instead. Before launching the target tool, sfs resume preflights the tool's project rules file from the current canonical SessionFS rules. Missing files are written; SessionFS-managed files are refreshed; unmanaged files are left alone with a warning on stderr unless --force-rules is passed. Preflight failures are non-fatal — resume still exits 0. See Resume-Time Rules Sync for the full policy. --model support per tool: Claude Code: passed as --model to the claude binary Codex: used in session injection and codex resume --model Gemini: passed as --model to the gemini binary Copilot: not supported (warns, uses Copilot's default) If omitted, each tool uses its own default model. Examples: $ sfs resume ses_abc123 --in codex Source session used rules v3 (sessionfs). Current project rules are v5. Synced codex.md from SessionFS rules v5. Launching codex resume ... Session resumed successfully. CC Session ID: abc123-def456 JSONL: /Users/me/.claude/projects/.../abc123-def456.jsonl Messages: 23 Skip preflight for a one-off resume: $ sfs resume ses_abc123 --in codex --no-rules-sync Take ownership of a hand-written codex.md: $ sfs resume ses_abc123 --in codex --force-rules

sections.heading: sfs checkpoint
sections.text: Create a named checkpoint of a session's current state. sfs checkpoint SESSION_ID --name NAME | Argument | Required | Description | | SESSION_ID | yes | Session ID or prefix | | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --name | string | required | Checkpoint name | Example: $ sfs checkpoint a1b2 --name "before-refactor" Checkpoint 'before-refactor' created for session a1b2c3d4e5f6.

sections.heading: sfs fork
sections.text: Fork a session into a new independent session. sfs fork SESSION_ID --name NAME [OPTIONS] | Argument | Required | Description | | SESSION_ID | yes | Session ID or prefix | | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --name | string | required | Title for the forked session | | --from-checkpoint | string | — | Fork from a named checkpoint instead of current state | Example: $ sfs fork a1b2 --name "Try different approach" Forked session created: f6e5d4c3b2a1 Title: Try different approach Parent: a1b2c3d4e5f6

sections.text: Import sessions from external sources. sfs import [FILE] [OPTIONS] | Argument | Required | Description | | FILE | no | File to import (for file-based import) | | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --from | string | — | Import source: claude-code | | --format | string | — | Input format (for file import) | Example: # Import all Claude Code sessions $ sfs import --from claude-code Found 47 Claude Code session(s). Imported 47 new session(s).

sections.heading: sfs daemon start
sections.text: Start the SessionFS daemon in the background. sfs daemon start [OPTIONS] | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --config | path | — | Path to config.toml | | --log-level | string | INFO | Log level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR | Example: $ sfs daemon start Daemon started (PID 12345). Logs: /Users/me/.sessionfs/daemon.log

sections.heading: sfs daemon stop
sections.text: Stop the running daemon. sfs daemon stop Example: $ sfs daemon stop Sent SIGTERM to daemon (PID 12345).

sections.heading: sfs daemon status
sections.text: Show daemon status and watcher health. sfs daemon status Example: $ sfs daemon status SessionFS Daemon Status ┌──────────────────┬────────────────────────┐ │ Field │ Value │ ├──────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ │ PID │ 12345 │ │ Running │ Yes │ │ Sessions │ 47 │ │ Watcher: cc │ healthy (47 sessions) │ └──────────────────┴────────────────────────┘ If pushes for a session keep failing (server errors, rate limits, network), the daemon backs off instead of retrying every cycle: after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 15 minutes, then hourly. After a long failing streak (12 attempts over at least six hours) it pauses that session until the session changes, the daemon restarts, or you run sfs daemon retry-sync. sfs daemon status lists these sessions with their failure count and last error, and sfs doctor reports them under "Sync retries".

sections.heading: sfs daemon retry-sync
sections.text: Retry sessions whose sync is backing off or paused after failed pushes, on the daemon's next sync cycle. sfs daemon retry-sync [SESSION_ID] | Argument / Option | Description | | SESSION_ID | Retry just this session (a unique prefix of its ID also works). Omit to retry every session that is backing off or paused. | | --config PATH | The config file the daemon was started with, if you started it with sfs daemon start --config. | Example: $ sfs daemon retry-sync ses_abc12345

sections.heading: sfs daemon logs
sections.text: Show daemon log output. sfs daemon logs [OPTIONS] | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --lines, -n | int | 50 | Number of lines to show | | --follow, -f | flag | false | Follow log output (like tail -f) | Example: $ sfs daemon logs -n 10 2026-03-20 14:30:00 sfsd INFO sfsd starting with 1 watcher(s) 2026-03-20 14:30:01 sfsd INFO sfsd running (PID 12345)

sections.heading: sfs config show
sections.text: Show the current configuration. sfs config show Example: $ sfs config show Config: /Users/me/.sessionfs/config.toml log_level = "INFO" scan_interval_s = 5.0 [claude_code] enabled = true

sections.heading: sfs config set
sections.text: Set a configuration value. sfs config set KEY VALUE | Argument | Required | Description | | KEY | yes | Config key (dotted path, e.g., claude_code.enabled) | | VALUE | yes | Value to set | Example: $ sfs config set scan_interval_s 10 Set scan_interval_s = 10

sections.heading: sfs config default-org
sections.text: Set or clear the server-canonical default organization used when capturing sessions and creating projects. Available starting v0.10.0. sfs config default-org [ORG_ID | --clear] | Argument | Required | Description | | ORG_ID | no | Org ID to use as default. Pass --clear to drop the preference. | The value is persisted on the server (users.default_org_id) and returned in GET /auth/me. Membership is validated — non-members cannot set an org as default. Example: $ sfs config default-org acme_eng Default organization set to acme_eng.

sections.heading: sfs alias
sections.text: Set or clear a session alias for easy reference. sfs alias SESSION_ID [ALIAS] | Argument | Required | Description | | SESSION_ID | yes | Session ID or prefix | | ALIAS | no | Alias name (omit to clear) | Example: $ sfs alias ses_a1b2 auth-debug Alias set: auth-debug -> ses_a1b2c3d4e5f6 $ sfs show auth-debug # Now works with alias

sections.heading: sfs search

sections.heading: sfs summary
sections.text: Show a session summary — files changed, tests run, commands executed. sfs summary SESSION_ID [OPTIONS] | Argument | Required | Description | | SESSION_ID | yes | Session ID or prefix | | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --format | string | — | Export format: md for markdown | Example: $ sfs summary ses_a1b2 Debug auth middleware 2.3h | 327 msgs | 28 tool calls | Claude Code Branch: feature/auth-fix @ a1b2c3d Files modified (3): src/auth/middleware.py src/auth/tokens.py tests/test_auth.py Commands: 34 Tests: 6 runs (5 passed, 1 failed) Packages: pyjwt, redis

sections.heading: sfs audit
sections.text: Audit a session for hallucinations using LLM-as-a-Judge. sfs audit SESSION_ID [OPTIONS] | Argument | Required | Description | | SESSION_ID | yes | Session ID or prefix | | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --model | string | claude-sonnet-4 | Judge LLM model | | --api-key | string | — | LLM API key (or use config/env) | | --provider | string | auto-detect | Provider: anthropic, openai, google, openrouter | | --base-url | string | — | Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama) | | --consensus | flag | false | Run 3 passes, report where 2+ agree (3x cost) | | --report | flag | false | Show existing report only | | --json | flag | false | Output as JSON | | --format | string | — | Export: json, markdown, csv | Example: $ sfs audit ses_a1b2 --model gpt-4o --base-url https://litellm.internal/v1 Trust Score: 74% 3 contradictions | 9 unverified | 42 verified CRITICAL test_result msg #34 "Test passes" -> exit code 1 HIGH file_existence msg #12 "Created validator.py" -> No Write call

sections.heading: sfs delete
sections.text: Delete a session from the cloud, the local device, or both. Requires an explicit scope flag -- there is no default. sfs delete SESSION_ID [OPTIONS] | Argument | Required | Description | | SESSION_ID | yes | Session ID or prefix | | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --cloud | flag | -- | Delete from server, keep local copy | | --local | flag | -- | Remove local copy, keep cloud copy | | --everywhere | flag | -- | Delete from both server and local | | --force | flag | false | Skip confirmation prompt | If no scope flag is provided, the command prints an error and exits. Examples: # Remove from cloud only (local copy stays) $ sfs delete ses_abc123 --cloud Delete ses_abc123 from cloud? Local copy will be kept. [y/N] y Deleted from cloud. Recoverable for 30 days. # Remove from this device only $ sfs delete ses_abc123 --local Delete ses_abc123 from this device? Cloud copy is unaffected. [y/N] y Removed local copy. # Delete everywhere (recoverable for 30 days) $ sfs delete ses_abc123 --everywhere --force Deleted from cloud and local device. Recoverable for 30 days. See Delete Lifecycle for full details on retention, recovery, and sync behavior.

sections.heading: sfs trash
sections.text: List soft-deleted sessions in the retention window. sfs trash Example: $ sfs trash Trash (3 sessions -- purge after 30 days) ID Deleted Scope Purge after ses_abc123 2 days ago cloud 2026-05-14 ses_def456 5 days ago everywhere 2026-05-11 ses_ghi789 12 days ago everywhere 2026-04-28

sections.heading: sfs restore
sections.text: Undo a soft-delete. Clears the server-side deletion flag and removes the session from the local exclusion list. sfs restore SESSION_ID | Argument | Required | Description | | SESSION_ID | yes | Session ID or prefix | If the local copy was also removed (scope was everywhere), run sfs pull <id> afterward to re-download it. Example: $ sfs restore ses_abc123 Session restored. Run 'sfs pull ses_abc123' to re-download locally.

sections.heading: sfs push
sections.text: Push a session to the cloud. sfs push SESSION_ID [--yes] [--timeout SECONDS] | Option | Description | | --yes, -y | Skip interactive confirmations (DLP findings, cloud-undelete). Findings are still shown. | | --timeout SECONDS | How long to wait for the server to accept the upload (1–3600). Defaults to SFS_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT, then upload_timeout under [sync] in config.toml, then 300. Raise it for very large sessions on servers that run DLP scans. | If the server doesn't answer in time, the push stops with a message saying so and how to raise the limit, instead of retrying the same upload.

sections.heading: sfs pull
sections.text: Pull a session from the cloud. sfs pull SESSION_ID Since v0.24.0 the local copy is replaced to match the server: files the server version no longer has are removed, while local-only reports such as the audit report and checkpoints are kept.

If neither flag is supplied, the project is personal-scope (pre-v0.10.0 behavior).

sections.heading: sfs project rebuild

Example: $ sfs project ask "How does session conflict resolution work?" ╭─ Question: How does session conflict resolution work? ─╮ ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ Matching Knowledge Entries (2): [decision] Sessions are append-only — conflict resolution appends both sides Session: ses_a1b2 | 2026-03-15 | confidence: 95% [pattern] Merge strategy: append both sides rather than 3-way merge Session: ses_c3d4 | 2026-03-10 | confidence: 90% Related Sessions: sfs show ses_a1b2 sfs show ses_c3d4 Save this Q&A to the knowledge base? [y/N]:

sections.heading: sfs project set
sections.text: Update project settings. sfs project set [OPTIONS] | Option | Type | Description | | --name | string | Rename the project (project-admin only). Available starting v0.12.1. | | --auto-narrative / --no-auto-narrative | flag | Enable or disable auto-narrative generation on sync | Example: $ sfs project set --auto-narrative auto_narrative = True $ sfs project set --name "Acme Platform" name = Acme Platform

sections.heading: sfs project dismiss

sections.heading: sfs project transfer
sections.text: Initiate, accept, reject, or cancel a project transfer between scopes (personal ↔ org, or org ↔ org). Available starting v0.10.0. sfs project transfer (--to TARGET | --accept ID | --reject ID | --cancel ID) [--force] | Option | Type | Description | | --to | string | Initiate a transfer to the given target. Use personal for personal scope, or an org ID for an org you belong to. | | --accept | string | Accept an incoming pending transfer by ID. | | --reject | string | Reject an incoming pending transfer by ID. | | --cancel | string | Cancel an outgoing pending transfer you initiated. | | --force | flag | With --to (auto-accepted) or --accept: transfer even if open tickets rely on org personas the destination lacks. | The transfer is auto-accepted when the initiator and target are the same user/org (e.g. moving a personal project into your own org). Standing is re-validated on accept/reject, so a member demoted between initiate and accept loses the right to act on the transfer. Org personas and transfers (GH #70): moving a project into a different org or out of one is refused (409 personas_stranded) when open tickets are assigned to org personas that will not exist in the destination; the error lists each persona and its ticket ids. Project personas move with the project, so a same-named project persona avoids the refusal. Nothing is copied automatically: reassign the tickets, create the personas in the destination, or pass --force (on --to when the transfer auto-accepts, or on --accept). Example: $ sfs project transfer --to acme_eng Transfer initiated. Awaiting target acceptance: xfer_a1b2c3

sections.heading: sfs project transfers
sections.text: List project transfers involving the caller. sfs project transfers [--direction incoming|outgoing] [--state pending|accepted|rejected|cancelled|expired] | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --direction | string | both | Filter by incoming or outgoing transfers | | --state | string | all | Filter by transfer state | A transfer proposed by an org admin (v0.23.0) appears in the project owner's incoming list labelled Proposed by <admin> for <org>: <reason> with its expiry, and in the proposer's outgoing list the same way. Accept or decline it with sfs project transfer --accept / --reject.

sections.heading: sfs project compile-schedule
sections.text: Set the scheduled knowledge-base compile for the current project (v0.23.0). sfs project show displays the current schedule. sfs project compile-schedule nightly sfs project compile-schedule weekly --after-claims 20 sfs project compile-schedule off sfs project compile-schedule weekly --no-after-claims | Argument / option | Type | Description | | schedule | off \| nightly \| weekly | How often the scheduled compile rebuilds the context document | | --after-claims | int | Also compile once this many claims are waiting, whatever the schedule (1+) | | --no-after-claims | flag | Clear the waiting-claims threshold so the project compiles only on schedule | nightly makes the project eligible every 24 hours, weekly every 7 days. off turns off the time-based schedule, but an --after-claims threshold still applies. Scheduled compiles use the deterministic compiler, never an LLM. On self-hosted servers the schedule takes effect only when something calls the compile sweep (see Self-Hosted).

sections.heading: sfs project group (Team+)

Every command addresses a group by its slug and takes --org (default: your default org); most take --json. sfs project list --group SLUG lists only that group's projects. See Project Groups. | Command | Description | | sfs project group list | The org's groups | | sfs project group create NAME [--slug S] [--description D] | Create a group (org admin or owner) | | sfs project group show GROUP | A group's members and projects | | sfs project group set GROUP [--name N] [--slug S] [--description D] [--compile\|--no-compile] | Rename or describe a group, or turn its overview compile on or off (group admin) | | sfs project group delete GROUP | Delete a group (org admin or owner) | | sfs project group add GROUP PROJECT_ID... | Add projects (group admin who can edit each project) | | sfs project group remove GROUP PROJECT_ID | Remove a project (group admin) | | sfs project group members GROUP | Members and their roles | | sfs project group grant GROUP USER --role reader\|editor\|admin | Grant or change a member's role; USER is an org member's email or user id (group admin) | | sfs project group revoke GROUP USER | Revoke a member's grant (group admin) | | sfs project group access | Every group you have access to, across your orgs | | sfs project group search GROUP [QUERY] [--entry-type T] [--limit N] | Search knowledge claims across the group's projects you can read (QUERY 3–200 characters; omit it to list top claims) | | sfs project group context GROUP | The group's compiled overview | | sfs project group compile GROUP | Compile the overview (group editor or admin; the group must have compile turned on) |

sections.heading: sfs project confluence publish (Enterprise)

See Confluence Cloud. sfs project confluence publish architecture --preview sfs project confluence publish --context --yes | Argument / option | Description | | slug | Wiki page slug to publish | | --context | Publish the project context document instead of a wiki page | | --preview | Show the draft, with its citations and anything dropped, without publishing | | --yes, -y | Skip the confirmation prompt |

sections.heading: sfs rules
sections.text: Manage canonical project rules and compile them into the tool-specific files each AI agent reads (CLAUDE.md, codex.md, .cursorrules, .github/copilot-instructions.md, GEMINI.md). See Rules Portability for the full reference.

sections.heading: sfs rules init
sections.text: Seed canonical rules for the current project. Detects the git remote, preselects enabled tools from existing rule files + recent tool usage, and optionally imports a single unmanaged rule file as the canonical seed. sfs rules init [--local-only] | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --local-only | flag | false | Gitignore the compiled rule files instead of committing them | Only the five v0.9.9-supported tools are preselected: claude-code, codex, cursor, copilot, gemini. The picker shows the reason for each preselection (file present, recent usage, or manual pick). Example: $ sfs rules init Detected rule files: CLAUDE.md (reason: file present) .cursorrules (reason: file present) Recent tool usage (last 90 days): codex (reason: recent usage) Enable these tools? [Y/n] Seeded canonical rules for myorg/my-project. Run 'sfs rules edit' to edit preferences, then 'sfs rules compile'.

sections.heading: sfs rules edit
sections.text: Open the canonical static_rules document in $EDITOR. sfs rules edit

sections.heading: sfs rules show
sections.text: Show current canonical version, enabled tools, knowledge/context injection config, and whether compiled outputs are in sync. sfs rules show Example: $ sfs rules show Project: myorg/my-project Canonical version: 4 Enabled tools: claude-code, codex, cursor, gemini Knowledge injection: on Types: convention, decision Budget: 2000 tokens Context injection: on Sections: overview, architecture Budget: 2000 tokens Compiled outputs: in sync (last compile: 2026-04-12)

sections.heading: sfs rules compile
sections.text: Compile canonical rules into tool-specific files. Deterministic — no new version is created unless a compiled output changes by hash. sfs rules compile [--tool TOOL] [--dry-run] [--force] | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --tool | string | — | Compile for a single tool only | | --dry-run | flag | false | Show what would be written without touching disk | | --force | flag | false | Overwrite files not managed by SessionFS | Example: $ sfs rules compile Compiling canonical rules v4... CLAUDE.md written (sha256:9a1c…) codex.md written (sha256:4e2f…) .cursorrules written (sha256:b7d1…) .github/copilot-instructions.md written (sha256:c3a8…) GEMINI.md written (sha256:5f90…) New rules version: 5 SessionFS refuses to overwrite a rule file that is not managed (no SessionFS marker and not created by sfs rules init). Use sfs rules init to import it, or pass --force.

sections.heading: sfs rules push
sections.text: Push the canonical record and latest compiled version to the SessionFS API. Uses optimistic concurrency — a stale write returns 409 Conflict. sfs rules push

sections.heading: sfs rules pull
sections.text: Pull canonical rules from the SessionFS API. Run sfs rules compile afterwards to regenerate tool files. sfs rules pull

sections.heading: sfs rules emit
sections.text: Print the latest compiled rules for a tool to stdout. Reads from the local rule cache populated by sfs rules compile and sfs rules pull — never hits the network. sfs rules emit --tool TOOL [--format hook|file] | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --tool | string | required | Target tool (claude-code, codex, cursor, copilot, gemini) | | --format | string | hook | hook for Claude Code's hook JSON spec, file for the plain compiled body | --format hook is the format the SessionStart hook installed by sfs hooks install consumes. --format file is useful for piping the compiled body into another tool or inspecting it from the shell. If the local cache is empty, the command prints an empty payload and exits 0 — it never breaks Claude Code startup. Example: $ sfs rules emit --tool claude-code --format hook { "hookSpecificOutput": { "hookEventName": "SessionStart", "additionalContext": "..." } }

sections.heading: sfs hooks
sections.text: Manage SessionFS hooks for tools with native hook support. v0.10.1 supports Claude Code only. See Hook-based injection for the full reference.

sections.heading: sfs hooks install
sections.text: Wire the SessionFS SessionStart hook into the target tool's settings. The hook calls sfs rules emit on every session start and pipes the compiled rules into the system prompt. Idempotent — running twice does not duplicate the entry. sfs hooks install --for TOOL [--user|--project] [--force] | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --for | string | required | Target tool (claude-code only in v0.10.1) | | --user | flag | default | Install at user scope (~/.claude/settings.json) | | --project | flag | false | Install at project scope (.claude/settings.json in repo root) | | --force | flag | false | Skip the conflict warning when a managed CLAUDE.md already exists | Example: $ sfs hooks install --for claude-code Hook installed: ~/.claude/settings.json (SessionStart) SessionFS will inject project rules at every Claude Code startup.

sections.heading: sfs hooks uninstall
sections.text: Remove the SessionFS-managed hook entry from the target tool's settings. Idempotent — no-op if not installed. sfs hooks uninstall --for TOOL [--user|--project] [--force] | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --for | string | required | Target tool (claude-code only in v0.10.1) | | --user | flag | default | Uninstall from user scope | | --project | flag | false | Uninstall from project scope | | --force | flag | false | Skip the confirmation prompt |

sections.heading: sfs hooks status
sections.text: Show which SessionFS hooks are installed across supported tools and scopes. Tools without native hook support appear as N/A. sfs hooks status Example: $ sfs hooks status SessionFS Hooks ─────────────── claude-code (user): INSTALLED at ~/.claude/settings.json (SessionStart) claude-code (project): not installed codex: N/A (no native hook system) gemini: N/A cursor: N/A

sections.heading: sfs mcp serve
sections.text: Start the MCP server on stdio transport. sfs mcp serve Tools exposed: 115, covering sessions (including ask_session_helper), knowledge, rules, personas, tickets (including watch_ticket and get_ticket_updates), agent runs (including replay_agent_run, report_agent_run_usage and get_spend_summary), review-loop rollups (get_loop_report), merge readiness (check_merge_readiness), review loops (start_review_loop, get_loop_status and update_review_loop), the review checklist (get_loop_checklist and propose_checklist_item), agent feedback, handoffs, work queues, the skills marketplace, project groups and meetings. Also injects knowledge-contribution instructions into the tool's project config file. sfs mcp install --for TOOL [OPTIONS] | Option | Type | Description | | --for | string | Target tool: claude-code, codex, gemini, cursor, copilot, amp, cline, roo-code, kilo-code, antigravity | | --skip-instructions | flag | Skip injecting knowledge-contribution instructions into project config | Example: $ sfs mcp install --for claude-code Added SessionFS MCP server in Claude Code. Restart Cursor to apply. Removed knowledge instructions from .cursorrules

Detects installed AI coding tools, writes configuration, optionally sets up cloud sync, and starts the daemon. sfs init Detects: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Amp, Cline, Roo Code, Kilo Code, Antigravity. Example: $ sfs init SessionFS Setup Scanning for AI coding tools... ✓ Claude Code detected (~/.claude) ✓ Cursor detected (~/Library/Application Support/Cursor) ✓ Gemini CLI detected (~/.gemini) ✗ Codex not found Found 3 tools.
